chunks: The king said: 'Bring him to me.' So when the messenger came to him, he said: 'Go back to your lord and ask him: What is the matter with the women who cut their hands? Indeed, my Lord is cognizant of their guile.'
ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Joseph tell the messenger to ask the King about the women who cut their hands?
ai.summary: In this verse, Prophet Joseph (AS) responds to the Egyptian king's summons by directing the messenger to inquire about the women who cut their hands, thereby shifting the focus from his own beauty to their deceptive plot. This response highlights his divine wisdom and confidence, as he asserts that God is fully aware of their cunning (*kaydihin*), a key theme in the narrative of Surah Yusuf. The verse underscores the contrast between human perception and divine knowledge, a central motif in Shia exegesis regarding Joseph's trials.
